cells.remarks: Registers a renewal by king Bhāskaravarmman, of a grant of land made by his ancestor Bhūtivarmman to a Brāhmaṇa Ghōshasvāmin and other Brāhmaṇas of various gōtras and sūtras. A list of the new donees who were apparently descended from the earlier recipients is given. Bhāskaravarmman's genealogy is traced from Naraka, born of Vishṇu and Bhūdēvi. He is stated to be the younger brother of Susthitavarmman and both the brothers are described to have fought a sanguinary battle against the Gauḍas in which they were defeated and taken prisoners but regained their kingdom later. Published in Epigraphia Indica, Vol. XXX, No. 47.

cells.remarks: The grant consists of 55 plates falling into three groups. The first comprising three plates is entirely in Sanskrit written in Grantha characters. It gives the genealogy of the Chōḷa family upto Rājēndra Chōḷa I and the details of the gift of the village Tribhuvanamahādēvi-chaturvēdimangalam to a number of Brāhmaṇas. The second group consists of 22 plates and in Tamil language. It starts by referring to the king by the title Kōnērimai-koṇḍān and quotes the regnal year as the 107th day. It gives details of lands granted to Tribhu- vanamahādēvi-chaturvēdimangalam after which the king is introduced with his praśasti commencing with the words, Tirumaṇi-valara, etc. It concludes by mentioning the boundaries of the gift village and the officials connected with the grant. The third group consists of 30 plates, Tamil, containing the names of the Brāhmaṇa donees of the village Tribhuvanamahādēvi-chaturvēdimangalam.
